title: Daily Life - Complaining at a Restaurant
audio: mp3/107. Daily Life - Complaining at a Restaurant.mp3

segments.en: Hello English learners, welcome back to another great podcast here at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 您好英语学习者，欢迎回到 Englishpod 的另一个很棒的播客。

segments.en: And today we're going to be talking about one of our favorite topics as always.
segments.zh: 今天我们将一如既往地谈论我们最喜欢的话题之一。

segments.en: We're going to be at a restaurant.
And, you know, one of the most difficult or embarrassing things to deal with at a restaurant is what to say when you don't like the food or when it's bad quality food.
segments.zh: 而且，你知道，在餐厅处理最困难或最尴尬的事情之一就是当你不喜欢食物或质量差的食物时该说些什么。

segments.en: So maybe we have to complain about the food or maybe even the service, right?
segments.zh: 所以也许我们不得不抱怨食物甚至服务，对吧？

segments.en: And in this lesson, we're going to be learning some really wonderful words and phrases that you can use when you need to complain about the food or the service in a restaurant.
segments.zh: 在本课中，我们将学习一些非常棒的单词和短语，当您需要抱怨餐厅的食物或服务时，您可以使用这些单词和短语。

segments.en: So before we listen to what happens in this restaurant with this food, let's take a look very quickly at vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 因此，在我们聆听这家餐厅用这种食物发生的事情之前，让我们快速看看词汇预览。

segments.en: We're only going to do one word today.
And this you'll hear in the dialogue.
So when I say an establishment, that's a noun.
segments.zh: 所以当我说一个机构时，这是一个名词。

segments.en: It's basically a fancy word for a business or a restaurant in this case.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，它基本上是企业或餐厅的花哨词。

segments.en: In this case, it's a restaurant.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，它是一家餐馆。

segments.en: But in general, you can say it's a business.
segments.zh: 但总的来说，你可以说这是一门生意。

segments.en: So you have a very fine establishment.
segments.zh: 所以你有一个非常好的机构。

segments.en: So an establishment, a type of business, a place of business, really.
segments.zh: 所以一个机构，一种商业类型，一个商业场所，真的。

segments.en: So now it's time for us to listen to our dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以现在是我们聆听对话的时候了。

segments.en: We're going to find out what's going on here.
segments.zh: 我们将在这里了解发生了什么。

segments.en: Apparently, there is a very angry customer and we're going to find out why.
segments.zh: 显然，有一个非常愤怒的客户，我们将找出原因。

segments.en: What can I do for you?
I've been sitting here for the past 20 minutes and no one has offered me a glass of water, brought any bread to the table, and our appetizers haven't been served yet.
segments.zh: 我在这儿坐了二十分钟，没人倒水，也没上面包，前菜还没来。

segments.en: You know, in this kind of establishment, I'd expect much better service.
segments.zh: 这种档次的餐厅，服务本该好得多。

segments.en: I'll check on your order right away.
The place is busy tonight and I've heard the food is amazing.
segments.zh: 今晚客人多，而且我听说这儿的菜特别好吃。

segments.en: The foie gras for the lady and a mushroom soup for you.
segments.zh: 女士的是鹅肝，您的是蘑菇汤。

segments.en: I ordered a cream of mushroom soup with asparagus.
segments.zh: 我点的是奶油蘑菇芦笋汤。

segments.en: The soup is obviously too runny and it's over seasoned.
segments.zh: 这汤太稀了，调味也太重。

segments.en: Can I bring you another soup or would you like to order something else?
segments.zh: 给您换一份汤，还是您想改点别的？

segments.en: Take this foie gras back as well.

segments.zh: 鹅肝又老又韧，完全做过火了。

segments.en: And look at the portion size.
How can you charge $25 for a sliver of duck liver?
segments.zh: 就这么薄薄一片鸭肝，你们敢收二十五美元？

segments.en: Why are you making such a big deal?
Are you trying to get our meal comped again?
segments.zh: 你又想让餐厅给我们免单吗？

segments.en: We're paying for this and I'm shelling out my hard earned bucks.
segments.zh: 这顿饭可是我掏钱，我花的是辛辛苦苦挣来的钱。

segments.en: I hope it is all right now.
The chef has prepared it especially for you.
segments.zh: 主厨特意为您重新做的。

segments.en: Well I guess that's one lesson.
Hey, if you're in a restaurant, don't be too rude to the waiter.
segments.zh: 嘿，如果你在餐厅，不要对服务员太粗鲁。

segments.en: You never know what's going to happen.
segments.zh: 你永远不知道会发生什么。

segments.en: The waiter and the cook, right?
Yeah, you don't want to offend that kitchen staff.
segments.zh: 是的，你不想冒犯那些厨房工作人员。

segments.en: So we'll talk about that a little bit later on but now I think we had some really interesting vocabulary of how to describe food that is not well prepared and we can take a look at that now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以我们稍后会讨论这个问题，但现在我认为我们有一些非常有趣的词汇来描述没有充分准备的食物，我们现在可以在语言外卖中看看。

segments.en: All right, so the guy in this dialogue, he ordered a mushroom soup and he complained that the mushroom soup was too runny.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以在这次对话中的那个人，他点了一份蘑菇汤，他抱怨蘑菇汤太稀了。

segments.en: Okay, the soup is too runny.
So he wanted a cream of mushroom so it should be a little bit thicker.
segments.zh: 所以他想要一个奶油蘑菇，所以它应该更厚一点。

segments.en: But in this case, it was runny.
segments.zh: 但在这种情况下，它是流失的。

segments.en: So when something is runny, it's too liquid.
segments.zh: 因此，当某物流失时，它太液体了。

segments.en: And I think we can relate it to a runny nose, right?
segments.zh: 我认为我们可以将它与流鼻涕联系起来，对吧？

segments.en: Okay, so when liquid is coming out of your nose, a runny nose, in this case, the soup is runny.
segments.zh: 好的，所以当液体从你的鼻子里流出来时，流鼻涕，在这种情况下，汤是流动的。

segments.en: And another thing that he was complaining about, the food was over seasoned.
segments.zh: 还有他在抱怨的另一件事，食物已经调味了。

segments.en: Okay, so if the food is over seasoned.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果食物过于调味。

segments.en: So it's another way of saying it's too salty.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一种说法，它太咸了。

segments.en: Yeah, it's kind of a fancy cooking term.
segments.zh: 是的，这是一个花哨的烹饪术语。

segments.en: Now can I say if there's too much pepper in the food, can I say it's over seasoned?
segments.zh: 现在我可以说如果食物中有太多的胡椒粉，我可以说它已经调味过了吗？

segments.en: When a cook says something is over seasoned, he's talking salt only.
segments.zh: 当厨师说某事过味时，他只是在说盐。

segments.en: So the cream of mushroom is very runny, it's over seasoned, and he said it's completely inedible.
segments.zh: 所以蘑菇的奶油很流，它已经过味了，他说它完全不能食用。

segments.en: So we have this prefix inedible.
segments.zh: 所以我们有这个前缀不可食用。

segments.en: And it doesn't mean that physically you can't eat it.
segments.zh: 这并不意味着你不能吃它。

segments.en: It just means it's pretty disgusting.
segments.zh: 这只是意味着它非常恶心。
这种食物是不可食用的。

segments.en: And then he started to complain about the other dish and he said that it's rubbery.
segments.zh: 然后他开始抱怨另一道菜，他说它是橡胶状的。

segments.en: So I think we noticed the word rubber.
segments.zh: 所以我想我们注意到了橡胶这个词。

segments.en: So obviously if a food is rubbery, it's too chewy.
segments.zh: 所以很明显，如果食物是橡胶状的，它太耐嚼了。

segments.en: It's like chewing on the bottom of your shoe, right?
segments.zh: 这就像在你的鞋底咀嚼，对吧？

segments.en: Okay, so it's too hard to chew or to swallow.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以咀嚼或吞咽太难了。

segments.en: And apparently the food was rubbery because it's completely overcooked.
segments.zh: 显然食物是橡胶状的，因为它完全煮过头了。

segments.en: So when something is overcooked, I mean it's easy to understand that it's cooked too much.
segments.zh: 所以当东西煮过头时，我的意思是很容易理解它煮得太多了。

segments.en: But it doesn't mean that it's burnt, right?
segments.zh: 但这并不意味着它被烧毁了，对吧？

segments.en: So maybe you've ordered your steak to be rare, but it comes to you well done.
segments.zh: 所以也许你已经订购了你的牛排是罕见的，但它对你来说做得很好。

segments.en: So it's not burnt, but it's cooked too much.
segments.zh: 所以它没有烧焦，但煮得太多了。

segments.en: So also I guess we can say like chicken.
segments.zh: 所以我想我们可以说像鸡肉。

segments.en: Sometimes if you overcook chicken, it comes out too dry.
segments.zh: 有时如果你把鸡肉煮过头，它会变得太干。

segments.en: And finally he was complaining about the size of the dish and he said, this is a sliver of duck liver.
segments.zh: 最后他在抱怨这道菜的大小，他说，这是一片鸭肝。

segments.en: Now this word sliver is like a slice, right?
segments.zh: 现在这个词sliver就像一个切片，对吧？

segments.en: A very small, tiny little slice.
segments.zh: 一个非常小的，很小的一小片。

segments.en: So we can say, okay, I just want a sliver of bacon for breakfast.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以说，好吧，我只想要一小片培根作为早餐。

segments.en: Let's look at a few more examples of how we can use sliver.
segments.zh: 让我们看看如何使用 Sliver 的更多示例。

segments.en: He'll just have a sliver of cake and no ice cream.
segments.zh: 他只会吃一块蛋糕，没有冰淇淋。

segments.en: I'm really full, but it looks so delicious.
segments.zh: 我真的很饱，但它看起来很美味。

segments.en: Can you just cut me a sliver?
You call this sliver of beef on my plate a meal?
segments.zh: 你把我盘子里的这块牛肉叫做饭吗？

segments.en: And those are all the words we had for language takeaway.
segments.zh: 这些都是我们为语言外卖而说的所有词。

segments.en: Now you have, so we've given you different adjectives of describing food that is not well prepared.
segments.zh: 现在你有了，所以我们给了你描述没有充分准备的食物的不同形容词。

segments.en: So now let's move on to some other phrases that the customer used to complain in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们继续讨论客户在 Flueny Builder 中抱怨的其他短语。

segments.en: So before we get to the customer complaining language, I want to look at a phrase that the waiter used to apologize.
segments.zh: 因此，在我们联系到客户抱怨语言之前，我想看看服务员过去常常道歉的短语。

segments.en: Now, why is this phrase so interesting?
segments.zh: 现在，为什么这句话如此有趣？

segments.en: Well, I mean, it's pretty easy to understand the meaning, but I want to look at why he added this verb do.
segments.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，这很容易理解它的含义，但我想看看他为什么添加这个动词 do。

segments.en: Well, he added the verb do to this phrase to make it seem a little bit stronger, to give a little more power to his apology.
segments.zh: 好吧，他在这个短语上添加了动词 do，以使它看起来更强一些，为他的道歉赋予更多的力量。

segments.en: So if you have an affirmative phrase, like I apologize, it's good.
segments.zh: 所以如果你有一个肯定的短语，就像我道歉一样，这很好。

segments.en: If you want to give it a little bit more emphasis, you can say, I do apologize.
segments.zh: 如果你想多加一点强调，你可以说，我很抱歉。

segments.en: Why don't we give an example?
segments.zh: 我们为什么不举个例子？

segments.en: So I might say this, Marco, I didn't know we had a party tonight.
segments.zh: 所以我可能会这么说，马可，我不知道我们今晚有一个派对。

segments.en: I did tell you about it last week.
So you're just giving a little bit more power to the statement that you told me.
segments.zh: 所以你只是给你告诉我的陈述更多的力量。

segments.en: So this do, did, does, becomes an auxiliary to make it more powerful, to give it more emphasis.
segments.zh: 所以，做，做，做，成为使它更强大的辅助，赋予它更多的强调。

segments.en: And a neat little phrase, something you can use if you want to make your apologies sound maybe a little bit stronger.
segments.zh: 还有一个整洁的小短语，如果你想让你的道歉听起来可能更强烈，你可以使用一些东西。

segments.en: Now moving on to the next phrase, he was complaining about the food and it was terrible.
segments.zh: 现在继续下一个短语，他在抱怨食物，这很糟糕。

segments.en: And he said, I'm shelling out my hard earned bucks.
segments.zh: 他说，我要花掉我辛苦赚来的钱。

segments.en: Okay, let's break this one down into two sections.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们把这个分成两个部分。

segments.en: So when you shell out, you pay for something.
segments.zh: 所以当你花钱时，你会付钱。

segments.en: So this gives you the sensation that you are, that you don't really want to pay.
segments.zh: 所以这给你一种感觉，你真的不想付钱。

segments.en: You're a bit unhappy about it.
So you want to shell out your money.
Why don't we listen to some examples to show us how we can use this phrase to shell out.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不听一些例子来向我们展示如何使用这个短语来表达。

segments.en: It's my girlfriend's birthday this month.
segments.zh: 这个月是我女朋友的生日。

segments.en: So I'm going to have to shell out for a present.
segments.zh: 所以我将不得不花钱买礼物。

segments.en: I really want those shoes, but I can't really afford to shell out $400.
segments.zh: 我真的很想要那些鞋子，但我真的买不起 400 美元。

segments.en: Ella shelled out the 800 bucks for the tickets.
segments.zh: 艾拉花了 800 美元买票。

segments.en: I thought I would have to pay.
So now that we understand shell out, let's move on to the second part of that sentence.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们了解了 shell out，让我们继续讨论这句话的第二部分。

segments.en: But his hard earned bucks is money he had to work really hard for.
segments.zh: 但他辛苦赚来的钱是他必须努力工作的钱。

segments.en: So I can also say my hard earned money, right?
segments.zh: 所以我也可以说我辛苦赚来的钱，对吧？
或者我辛苦赚来的现金。

segments.en: So you worked hard to get it.
So three great phrases that can be used when you're complaining in a restaurant.
segments.zh: 因此，当您在餐厅抱怨时，可以使用三个很棒的短语。

segments.en: Why don't we hear them one last time in context by listening to the dialogue.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不通过听对话最后一次在上下文中听到他们的声音。

segments.en: What can I do for you?
I've been sitting here for the past 20 minutes and no one has offered me a glass of water, brought any bread to the table, and our appetizers haven't been served yet.
segments.zh: 我在这儿坐了二十分钟，没人倒水，也没上面包，前菜还没来。

segments.en: You know, in this kind of establishment, I'd expect much better service.
segments.zh: 这种档次的餐厅，服务本该好得多。

segments.en: I'll check on your order right away.
The place is busy tonight and I've heard the food is amazing.
segments.zh: 今晚客人多，而且我听说这儿的菜特别好吃。

segments.en: The foie gras for the lady and a mushroom soup for you.
segments.zh: 女士的是鹅肝，您的是蘑菇汤。

segments.en: I ordered a cream of mushroom soup with asparagus.
segments.zh: 我点的是奶油蘑菇芦笋汤。

segments.en: The soup is obviously too runny and it's over seasoned.
segments.zh: 这汤太稀了，调味也太重。

segments.en: Okay, I do apologize for that.
Can I bring you another soup or would you like to order something else?
segments.zh: 给您换一份汤，还是您想改点别的？

segments.en: Take this foie gras back as well.

segments.zh: 鹅肝又老又韧，完全做过火了。

segments.en: And look at the portion size.
How can you charge $25 for a sliver of duck liver?
segments.zh: 就这么薄薄一片鸭肝，你们敢收二十五美元？

segments.en: Why are you making such a big deal?
Are you trying to get our meal comped again?
segments.zh: 你想让我们的饭菜再次得到补偿吗？

segments.en: We're paying for this and I'm shelling out my hard earned bucks.
segments.zh: 这顿饭可是我掏钱，我花的是辛辛苦苦挣来的钱。

segments.en: I hope it is all right now.
The chef has prepared it especially for you.
segments.zh: 主厨特意为您重新做的。

segments.en: So complaining at a restaurant and actually sending food back is not uncommon in the US.
segments.zh: 因此，在餐厅抱怨并实际将食物送回去在美国并不少见。

segments.en: If the food's bad, of course you're going to send it back.
segments.zh: 如果食物不好，你当然会把它寄回去。

segments.en: But maybe in other cultures, I think people would be a little bit more reluctant to do something like this.
segments.zh: 但也许在其他文化中，我认为人们会更不愿意做这样的事情。

segments.en: But hey, you know what's an interesting thing about the way Americans eat in restaurants is sometimes at the end of the meal, if they haven't finished everything, they might ask for a doggy bag.
segments.zh: 但是，嘿，你知道美国人在餐馆吃饭的方式有什么有趣的事情，如果他们还没有吃完所有东西，他们可能会要一个狗袋。

segments.en: So what is that, a doggy bag?

Well, usually if you order a big meal or half your steak is left over on your plate, you would ask for a doggy bag and they would bring you a little box or a bag and you would take it to supposedly give it to your dog.
segments.zh: 好吧，通常如果你点了一顿大餐或你的盘子里剩下一半的牛排，你会要一个小狗袋，他们会给你带来一个小盒子或一个袋子，你会把它送给你的狗。

segments.en: So it's sort of like you tell the waiter, oh, the steak was so good, I couldn't finish it, can I take some home to my dog?
segments.zh: 所以这有点像你告诉服务员，哦，牛排太好吃了，我没吃完，我可以带一些回家给我的狗吗？

segments.en: So you would just ask, waiter, can I have a doggy bag?
segments.zh: 所以你会问，服务员，我可以要一个狗袋吗？

segments.en: But it's sort of like code for I'm going to eat this tomorrow for lunch.
segments.zh: 但这有点像代码，因为我明天午餐要吃这个。

segments.en: So people wouldn't really give it to their dog.
segments.zh: 所以人们不会真的把它给他们的狗。

segments.en: You know, that steak wrapped up in a fancy sort of foil salon is going to be a pretty delicious the next day.
segments.zh: 你知道，包裹在花哨的箔沙龙中的牛排第二天会非常美味。

segments.en: It's actually very common in the US, but in other countries, people will leave entire plates of food on the table.
segments.zh: 这在美国实际上很常见，但在其他国家，人们会把整盘食物留在桌子上。

segments.en: It would be totally impolite to ask the waiter to pack up the food for you.
segments.zh: 让服务员为你收拾食物是完全不礼貌的。

segments.en: So a little bit of cultural differences, but we want to know what you think and how things are done maybe in your country with complaining or sending food back or even this whole doggy bag situation.
segments.zh: 所以有点文化差异，但我们想知道你的想法以及在你的国家是如何完成的，可能会抱怨或寄回食物，甚至是整个狗袋的情况。

segments.en: Why don't you visit our website, EnglishPod.com and tell us about it.
segments.zh: 您为什么不访问我们的网站 Englishpod.com 并告诉我们。

segments.en: We'll be there to answer any questions or comments, but we got to go now.
segments.zh: 我们会在那里回答任何问题或意见，但我们现在必须走了。
